questions.explain: PHBV is a biodegradable polyester copolymer of 3-hydroxybutanoic and 3-hydroxypentanoic acids. Glycine + 6-aminohexanoic acid gives nylon-2-nylon-6, and ethylene glycol + phthalic acid gives non-biodegradable glyptal.
Nylon-6, made from caprolactam, resists biodegradation. Nylon-2-nylon-6 is biodegradable because its glycine units give peptide-like amide links.

questions.q: Which polymer, made from glycolic acid, was the first synthetic absorbable surgical suture (Dexon)?
questions.explain: Polyglycolic acid, –(O–CH₂–CO)ₙ–, is the simplest aliphatic polyester and was the first synthetic absorbable suture. PLA comes from lactic acid and PCL from ε-caprolactone.

questions.q: Polylactic acid slowly breaks down inside the body, whereas polythene persists for centuries. The best reason is that
options: PLA has ester links in the main chain that water and enzymes can hydrolyse; polythene has only C–C and C–H bonds
PLA is an addition polymer and polythene is a condensation polymer
PLA has a lower molecular mass than any polythene
Polythene contains amide links that enzymes cannot cleave
questions.explain: Biodegradable polymers carry hydrolysable ester or amide links in the backbone; PLA hydrolyses back to lactic acid, a normal metabolite. Polythene's C–C and C–H bonds cannot be attacked by water or enzymes.
